issues.description: The exercise contains conflicting specifications for the Farm.animals collection type: the UML in the problem statement declares animals as a List<Animal>, while the textual Part 3 explicitly requires using a Set implemented with a HashSet. The provided solution uses a List/ArrayList for the animals field, which contradicts the textual requirement to use a Set/HashSet. This inconsistency can confuse students about which collection type to implement and may lead to mismatches with automated tests or grading expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement (text and UML) to require a List/ArrayList if uniqueness is not required, or (B) change the solution (and any template hints) to use a Set<Animal> with a HashSet implementation, e.g. private Set<Animal> animals; initialized with new HashSet<>(); and adjust getter/setter signatures and any code that relies on List-specific behavior. Prefer preserving the textual requirement (use HashSet) if uniqueness of animals is intended.

issues.description: The collection type used to store animals in Farm is inconsistent across artifacts. The textual Part 3 requirement explicitly states the Farm should use a Set implemented with a HashSet (problem_statement.md lines 108-110), while the UML earlier in the same problem statement shows animals: List<Animal> (problem_statement.md lines 16-22). The solution implementation declares a List<Animal> and initializes it with an ArrayList (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 9-13). The template Farm.java leaves the field unimplemented but its TODO references implementing the Farm as described in the task (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 3-11). This mismatch (Set/HashSet vs List/ArrayList) creates a conceptual mapping burden: students are told to implement uniqueness via a Set but the provided solution uses a List, and the UML even shows List, causing confusion about the intended data structure and behavior (uniqueness of animals).
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the discrepancy by aligning all artifacts to the same collection type. Preferred fix (to match the explicit Part 3 requirement): change the Farm implementation and its getter/setter in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java to use Set<Animal> and initialize it with new HashSet<>() in the no-arg constructor; update method signatures and any iteration accordingly. Also update the UML in problem_statement.md to show animals: Set<Animal> (or adjust the textual requirement if List is intended).
